changeLog.note: First registry (REV 16.1 Step 0). Moved every health threshold, schedule and safety wording out of Swift and index.html into this file.

Added the numbers behind Body Check: waist-to-height bands (NICE NG246) and the NHS half-height line, waist action levels (BMJ 1995), body-fat circumference method (US DoD), resting energy (Mifflin-St Jeor).

Added the numbers behind Body Age, the fitness tests and My Plan: waist-to-hip cut-off (WHO), cardio fitness by age (FRIEND registry), 1-minute sit-to-stand by age (Strassmann 2013), one-leg balance by age (Springer 2007), 30-second chair stand (CDC STEADI), weekly activity targets (CDC).

REV 17.1 Voice Coach: official protocol blocks for one-leg balance (Springer 2007) and 30-second chair stand (CDC STEADI), each line tied to a word-for-word quote verified live; 1-minute sit-to-stand protocol marked not verified (tap-only); coach wording entry.

values.formula: weight in kg divided by height in metres squared

entries.meaning: Adult (20+) BMI category cutoffs shown beside the BMI read from Apple Health. A screening measure, not a diagnosis.
entries.issuer: CDC
entries.note: Class 1/2/3 obesity splits (35, 40) exist at the source; the app shows one Obesity range.

entries.meaning: Global Solar UV Index exposure categories and their colour code, used for the widget's UV number, level word and colour.
entries.issuer: WHO / WMO / UNEP / ICNIRP (Global Solar UV Index)
entries.sourceVersionDate: Global Solar UVI 2002; Review workshop report 2017 (page undated)
entries.note: WHO's own Q&A (2022) groups the same scale into 0-2, 3-7, 8+ with advice; the five-band table is the global index. Hex values are the app's rendering of the official colour names.

entries.meaning: The ABCDE warning signs of melanoma shown on Findings when a spot has changed.
entries.issuer: American Academy of Dermatology
entries.note: The source describes D as usually greater than 6 mm; the app shows the word only and never states a size.

values.label: Monthly
values.shortText: Monthly is what the Skin Cancer Foundation recommends.
values.whyText: The Skin Cancer Foundation recommends a head-to-toe self-exam every month and a dermatologist full-body exam at least once a year.

entries.meaning: Default skin self-exam / scan reminder cadence and the wording that explains it.
entries.issuer: Skin Cancer Foundation
entries.note: More frequent cadences in Settings (every 2 weeks, weekly) are the user's choice, not guidance.

entries.meaning: Professional full-body skin exam interval used for the yearly dermatologist reminder.
entries.issuer: Skin Cancer Foundation
entries.note: The 2-week lead time before the anniversary is the app's own nudge, not guidance.

entries.meaning: Waist-to-height ratio bands for adults: healthy 0.4 to 0.49, increased 0.5 to 0.59, high 0.6 or more.
entries.issuer: NICE (NG246)
entries.note: NICE words the bands as central adiposity with no / increased / further increased health risks. The app shows only the band names plus the consult bar.

values.text: Keep your waist under half your height.

entries.meaning: The one-line waist-to-height advice shown with the ratio.
entries.issuer: NHS (Obesity)
entries.note: NHS states: try to keep your waist size to less than half your height.

entries.meaning: Waist circumference action levels: at or above the first number, gain no further weight; at or above the second, reduce weight.
entries.issuer: BMJ 1995 (Lean, Han, Morrison): Waist circumference as a measure for indicating need for weight management
entries.note: Original peer-reviewed source of the 94/102 cm (men) and 80/88 cm (women) action levels; the NHS page no longer lists them.

entries.meaning: US DoD circumference body-fat estimate (Navy method): men = 86.010 x log10(waist - neck) - 70.041 x log10(height) + 36.76; women = 163.205 x log10(waist + hip - neck) - 97.684 x log10(height) - 78.387; measurements in inches (the app converts from cm).
entries.issuer: US Dept of Defense (Hodgdon & Beckett 1984; Hodgdon & Friedl 1999), as reproduced in Foulis et al., Frontiers in Physiology 2023
entries.note: An estimate. The same article reports circumference methods do not reliably capture small body-composition changes, so the app labels it an estimate and does not rate it.

entries.meaning: Mifflin-St Jeor resting energy: 9.99 x weight(kg) + 6.25 x height(cm) - 4.92 x age + 166 x sex (male 1, female 0) - 161, in kcal per day.
entries.issuer: Mifflin MD, St Jeor ST et al., Am J Clin Nutr 1990;51:241-247 (PubMed 2305711)
entries.note: A population estimate of resting energy use in healthy adults, not a measurement.

labels.atOrAbove: At or above the WHO cut-off

entries.meaning: Waist-to-hip ratio (waist divided by hips). WHO cut-off: 0.90 or more for men, 0.85 or more for women.
entries.issuer: World Health Organization: Waist circumference and waist-hip ratio, report of a WHO expert consultation (Geneva, 8-11 December 2008)
entries.note: WHO lists these cut-offs with the wording 'substantially increased' risk of metabolic complications. The app shows the cut-off and the consult bar, never a disease.

entries.meaning: Cardio fitness (VO2 max) reference values by age and sex: 25th, 50th (median) and 75th percentile from measured treadmill tests.
entries.issuer: Kaminsky LA, Arena R, Myers J. Reference Standards for Cardiorespiratory Fitness Measured With Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing: Data From the FRIEND Registry. Mayo Clin Proc 2015;90(11):1515-1523
entries.note: US adults without known heart disease, ages 20-79. The app reads VO2 max from Apple Health (an Apple Watch estimate) and compares it with these measured values. Checked through the US National Library of Medicine's PubMed Central record PMC4919021.

entries.meaning: 1-minute sit-to-stand test: how many times you stand up from a chair and sit back down in 60 seconds. 25th, 50th (median) and 75th percentile by age and sex.
entries.issuer: Strassmann A, et al. Population-based reference values for the 1-min sit-to-stand test. Int J Public Health 2013;58:949-953
entries.note: 6,926 adults in Switzerland, ages 20-79. Chair about 46 cm high with no arm rests, arms not used to push, legs fully straight at the top.

protocol.source: Strassmann A, et al. Int J Public Health 2013;58:949-953 (Methods)
protocol.reason: The test procedure is in the paper's Methods, which the publisher page shows only to subscribers, and the open copy (doc.rero.ch/record/316283) answers HTTP 410 Gone (RERO DOC closed). It cannot be re-checked live, so this test stays tap-only with no spoken coaching. Its reference values (Table 2) are still verified live.
verify: Population-based reference values for the 1-min sit-to-stand test

entries.meaning: One-leg stand, eyes open: the best of 3 tries, stopped at 45 seconds. Average time by age group.
entries.issuer: Springer BA, Marin R, Cyhan T, Roberts H, Gill NW. Normative values for the unipedal stance test with eyes open and closed. J Geriatr Phys Ther 2007;30(1):8-15
entries.note: 549 adults ages 18-99, arms crossed, barefoot. The study found no difference between men and women, so one average is used. The test stops at 45 seconds, so it cannot tell strong balancers apart.

protocol.source: Springer BA, et al. J Geriatr Phys Ther 2007;30(1):8-15, Methods: Study Design (eyes-open condition)

quotes.stand: Eligible subjects were asked to stand barefoot on the limb of their choice, with the other limb raised so that the raised foot was near but not touching the ankle of their stance limb.
quotes.eyes: Each subject was asked to focus on a spot on the wall at eye level in front of him, for the duration of the eyes open test.
quotes.arms: Prior to raising the limb, the subject was instructed to cross his arms over the chest.
quotes.start: Time commenced when the subject raised the foot off the floor.
quotes.stop: Time ended when the subject either: (1) used his arms (ie, uncrossed arms), (2) used the raised foot (moved it toward or away from the standing limb or touched the floor), (3) moved the weight-bearing foot to maintain his balance (ie, rotated foot on the ground), (4) a maximum of 45 seconds had elapsed, or (5) opened eyes on eyes closed trials.
quotes.trials: The procedure was repeated 3 times and each time was recorded on the data collection sheet.
quotes.rest: At least 5 minutes of rest were allowed between each trial set to avoid fatigue.
quotes.kept: For the inferential statistics, we report only the results of the best since that is how the test is used clinically.

protocol.scriptNote: The paper gives no words to read to the person, so each spoken line says only what the cited sentence requires, in plain words. plainWords lists the only word swaps used.

setup.text: Barefoot, standing, in front of a wall with a spot at eye level.

startPosition.text: Standing on both feet, arms crossed over the chest, looking at the spot.

instructions.say: Stand barefoot, on the leg of your choice.
Look at a spot on the wall at eye level, in front of you.
Cross your arms over your chest.
Raise the other foot, near but not touching your ankle.

startTrigger.text: Timing starts when the raised foot leaves the floor.

stopConditions.text: Raised foot moves toward or away from the standing leg
stopConditions.phrase: moved it toward or away from the standing limb

stopConditions.text: Standing foot moves to keep balance
stopConditions.phrase: moved the weight-bearing foot to maintain his balance
a maximum of 45 seconds had elapsed

safety.text: The study gives no safety instruction for the person tested.

entries.meaning: 30-second chair stand (ages 60 and up): stands in 30 seconds with arms crossed on the chest. A score under the number for your age and sex is below average.
entries.issuer: CDC STEADI (Stopping Elderly Accidents, Deaths & Injuries): 30-Second Chair Stand assessment
entries.note: CDC states a below average score indicates a risk for falls. The app shows the label and the consult bar.

protocol.source: CDC STEADI, Assessment: 30-Second Chair Stand (sheet dated 2017)

quotes.equipment: Equipment: A chair with a straight back without arm rests (seat 17” high), and a stopwatch.
quotes.i1: Sit in the middle of the chair.
quotes.i2: Place your hands on the opposite shoulder crossed, at the wrists.
quotes.i3: Keep your feet flat on the floor.
quotes.i4: Keep your back straight, and keep your arms against your chest.
quotes.i5: On “Go,” rise to a full standing position, then sit back down again.
quotes.arms: If the patient must use his/her arms to stand, stop the test. Record “0” for the number and score.
quotes.count: Count the number of times the patient comes to a full standing position in 30 seconds.
quotes.half: If the patient is over halfway to a standing position when 30 seconds have elapsed, count it as a stand.
quotes.safety: NOTE: Stand next to the patient for safety.

protocol.scriptNote: CDC prints the words to say (Instruct the patient: 1-6, and Go). They are read word for word.

setup.text: A chair with a straight back without arm rests (seat 17 inches high).

startPosition.text: Sitting in the middle of the chair, hands on the opposite shoulders crossed at the wrists, feet flat, back straight, arms against the chest.

instructions.say: Sit in the middle of the chair.
Place your hands on the opposite shoulder crossed, at the wrists.
Keep your feet flat on the floor.
Keep your back straight, and keep your arms against your chest.
On Go, rise to a full standing position, then sit back down again.

startTrigger.text: Timing starts on the word Go.

stopConditions.text: Arms used to stand: the test stops and the score is 0
stopConditions.phrase: must use his/her arms to stand, stop the test

countRule.text: Full standing positions in 30 seconds. Over halfway up when 30 seconds end counts as a stand.

safety.text: For safety, have someone stand next to you.

entries.meaning: Weekly activity for adults: at least 150 minutes of moderate activity (or 75 minutes vigorous) and at least 2 days of muscle-strengthening activity.
entries.issuer: CDC: Adult Activity, An Overview (Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans)
entries.note: My Plan builds its weekly targets from these numbers.
verify: 150 minutes of moderate-intensity physical activity a week
2 days of muscle-strengthening activity each week

entries.meaning: Weekly activity for adults 65 and older: the same 150 minutes and 2 strength days, plus activities to improve balance.
entries.issuer: CDC: Older Adult Activity, An Overview (Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans)
entries.note: My Plan adds balance practice to every week from this age.
verify: At least 150 minutes at moderate intensity
At least 2 days of activities that strengthen muscles

values.text: Body Age is the age whose typical result matches yours, averaged over the tests you have done. It is a motivational estimate, not a medical age.

entries.meaning: How Body Age is worked out: for each test with published age values (cardio fitness, 1-minute sit-to-stand, one-leg balance) the app finds the age whose typical result equals yours, then averages those ages equally. Tests you have not done are left out, never guessed.
entries.issuer: The Body Guard (own method, built only on the published reference values listed in this database)
entries.note: Typical result = the median (cardio, sit-to-stand) or the average (balance) of each age group, joined in a straight line between age-group midpoints. Results beyond the youngest or oldest group count as that group's age.

values.text: ALWAYS CONSULT WITH A LICENSED HEALTH CARE PROVIDER

entries.issuer: The Body Guard (own safety wording, set by B Rad 2026-10-01)
